claims.text: MT-DNN achieves a score of 82.7% on the GLUE benchmark, representing a 2.2% absolute improvement over BERT.
MT-DNN achieves an accuracy of 91.6% on the SNLI dataset.
MT-DNN achieves an accuracy of 95.0% on the SciTail dataset.
Formulating QNLI as a pairwise ranking task instead of binary classification improves performance.
MT-DNN combines multi-task learning across natural language understanding tasks with a pre-trained Transformer language model as shared lower layers.
MT-DNN incorporates the Stochastic Answer Network (SAN) answer module for pairwise text classification output layers.

evidence.description: MT-DNN pushes the GLUE benchmark to 82.7% (2.2% absolute improvement) over BERTLARGE on the GLUE test set.
Adapted MT-DNNLARGE model achieves a test accuracy of 91.6% on SNLI, outperforming previous state-of-the-art results.
Adapted MT-DNNLARGE model achieves a test accuracy of 95.0% on SciTail, outperforming previous state-of-the-art results.
ST-DNN fine-tuned on QNLI using pairwise ranking loss achieves 96.1% dev accuracy compared to BERT fine-tuned using cross-entropy achieving 90.5%.
The lower layers are shared across all tasks using a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder, while top layers represent task-specific outputs.
The design of the pairwise text classification output module follows the answer module of the stochastic answer network (SAN) using multi-step reasoning.

methodologies.name: Multi-Task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN)
methodologies.description: A representation learning framework combining BERT-based pre-trained Transformer text encodings with multi-task objective fine-tuning across distinct task types.
conditions: Dropout rate 0.1 for task-specific layers (0.3 for MNLI, 0.05 for CoLA)

limitations.text: Supervised deep neural network learning requires large amounts of task-specific labeled data, which is not always available.
MT-DNN tends to underfit small, unique datasets like CoLA during multi-task learning prior to task-specific fine-tuning.

future_work.text: Gaining a deeper understanding of model structure sharing in multi-task learning.
Developing more effective training methods that leverage relatedness among multiple tasks for fine-tuning and pre-training.
Exploring ways of incorporating text linguistic structure in an explicit and controllable manner.
Verifying whether MT-DNN is resilient against adversarial attacks.
